title: The Residual $288$ of the $E_8\timesωE_8$ Program as Adjoint-Lineage Scaffolding Labels: an Ontology, and the Status of the Bifermionic Lagrangian
summary: In the $E_8\timesωE_8$ octonionic unification program, each $E_8$ branches as $SU(3)_{st}\times E_6$, supplying one geometric $SU(3)_{st}$ per branch, while the split-complex unit $ω$ grades the visible and pre-gravitational branches; matter and gauge content is carried by $E_6\times E_6$, with chiral fermions realized as Cl(6) minimal-ideal spinors rather than $E_8$ representation components -- which places the chiral sector outside the Distler-Garibaldi no-go theorem. Comparing the 496-label two-branch adjoint reservoir with the 208 structures matched in the Generalized Trace Dynamics Lagrangian leaves a residual 288. We argue that this 288 is an adjoint-lineage representation-label ledger -- bookkeeping for the scaffolding -- and not a particle spectrum. The bifermionic seed is Hermitian, with $E_6$-covariant channels classified by $\bar{27}\otimes 27 = 1\oplus 78\oplus 650$: each branch's 78 supplies the gauge currents and a composite electroweak doublet, while the $E_6$ singlet is electroweak-inert. The charge-sum sector A is absent from the bare seed, and the 252 $SU(3)_{st}$-charged labels cannot be matter bilinears in any reservoir, conditional on the spinor ontology. The size of $E_8\timesωE_8$ is thus the dimension of a label ledger, not a count of particles; beyond the Standard Model, the framework's content is sterile neutrinos and a second composite scalar.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that in the $E_8\timesωE_8$ octonionic unification program, the 496-dimensional adjoint representation per branch functions as a label ledger for scaffolding rather than a particle count. Chiral fermions are realized as Cl(6) minimal-ideal spinors, bypassing the Distler-Garibaldi no-go theorem. The residual 288 labels are bookkeeping, not particles; beyond the Standard Model, only sterile neutrinos and a second composite scalar emerge.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the large adjoint representation size of $E_8\timesωE_8$ unification with observable particle content, addressing the Distler-Garibaldi no-go theorem by placing chiral fermions outside $E_8$ representation components via Cl(6) spinor ontology.
AI.method: Branching $E_8$ as $SU(3)_{st}\times E_6$ across two (visible and pre-gravitational) branches graded by split-complex unit $ω$; analyzing the bifermionic seed via $E_6$-covariant channel decomposition ($\bar{27}\otimes 27 = 1\oplus 78\oplus 650$); comparing 496-label adjoint reservoir with 208 matched structures in Generalized Trace Dynamics Lagrangian; categorizing residual 288 as adjoint-lineage representation-label ledger.
AI.result: The 496 per branch is a label ledger dimension, not particle count. The 252 $SU(3)_{st}$-charged labels cannot be matter bilinears under the spinor ontology. Beyond Standard Model content is limited to sterile neutrinos and a second composite scalar.
AI.conclusion: The $E_8\timesωE_8$ framework avoids over-prediction of particles; its large representation is bookkeeping, and the actual new physics beyond the Standard Model is minimal (sterile neutrinos + one composite scalar).

title: Constraining the real scalar singlet extension of the SM
summary: The real scalar singlet extension of the standard model provides a minimal framework in which the Higgs sector can realise a strong first-order electroweak phase transition and improve the stability of the electroweak vacuum. We combine the electroweak phase transition and high-scale vacuum stability with current and projected collider probes, including precision Higgs measurements, the Higgs trilinear coupling, EWPO and resonant searches for a heavy singlet-like scalar in $ZZ$ and di-Higgs final states. Focusing on a singlet heavier than the standard model Higgs, we find that there is parameter space compatible with a strong first-order electroweak phase transition for singlet-like scalar masses up to nearly 1 TeV. Deviations in the Higgs self-coupling can be larger than those in the Higgs--$Z$ coupling, making Higgs-potential measurements a key probe. We find that the HL-LHC will test a large fraction of the parameter space, while the FCC will provide ultimate discovery and model-discrimination capabilities.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the real scalar singlet extension of the Standard Model, combining electroweak phase transition, vacuum stability, and collider probes. It finds viable parameter space for strong first-order phase transition up to ~1 TeV singlet masses, with HL-LHC testing large regions and FCC offering full discovery potential.
AI.motivation: To study whether the real scalar singlet extension of the Standard Model can simultaneously achieve a strong first-order electroweak phase transition and high-scale vacuum stability, while being testable at current and future colliders.
AI.method: Combined analysis of electroweak phase transition, high-scale vacuum stability, precision Higgs measurements, Higgs trilinear coupling, electroweak precision observables (EWPO), and resonant searches for heavy singlet-like scalars in ZZ and di-Higgs final states, confronting theory with current and projected collider constraints.
AI.result: Parameter space compatible with strong first-order EWPT exists for singlet-like scalar masses up to nearly 1 TeV. Higgs self-coupling deviations can exceed those in Higgs-Z coupling. HL-LHC can test a large fraction of this parameter space, while FCC provides ultimate discovery and discrimination power.
AI.conclusion: The singlet extension remains viable for strong first-order EWPT up to high masses; Higgs-potential measurements are key; future colliders (HL-LHC, FCC) offer strong testing capabilities.

title: Directional dark matter signatures of the Large Magellanic Cloud
summary: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), the most massive satellite of the Milky Way (MW), can significantly perturb the local dark matter (DM) distribution. We study its impact on directional DM detection using the Auriga cosmological simulations of a MW analogue hosting an LMC analogue. We find that the LMC induces strong anisotropies in directional recoil signals, driven primarily by the non-zero mean azimuthal velocity of the local DM distribution. The characteristic ring-like feature predicted in the Standard Halo Model (SHM) for heavy DM and low recoil energies is strongly distorted, producing an asymmetric recoil pattern concentrated at preferred azimuthal angles. Differences between recoil maps for the MW-LMC analogue and the SHM reach up to $\sim80\%$ near the signal maximum. These distortions significantly enhance directional discovery prospects, reducing the number of events required to reject isotropy by nearly a factor of five for a 100 GeV DM particle in a near-future CYGNUS-like experiment, and by even larger factors for heavier DM. Our results highlight the importance of the LMC for interpreting and optimizing future directional DM searches.

AI.tldr: Using Auriga simulations, this paper shows that the LMC significantly distorts the local DM distribution, creating strong anisotropies in directional recoil signals. This distortion enhances directional detection prospects, reducing required events to reject isotropy by up to ~5x for 100 GeV DM in a future CYGNUS-like experiment.
AI.motivation: To study how the Large Magellanic Cloud, as the most massive MW satellite, perturbs the local dark matter distribution and impacts directional DM detection, given that most detection strategies assume the Standard Halo Model which ignores such perturbations.
AI.method: Used Auriga cosmological simulations of a MW analogue hosting an LMC analogue to analyze the LMC's impact on directional DM recoil signals, comparing results against the Standard Halo Model predictions.
AI.result: LMC induces strong anisotropies in directional recoil signals driven by non-zero mean azimuthal velocity of local DM. The SHM ring-like feature becomes asymmetric and concentrated at preferred azimuthal angles. Recoil map differences reach ~80% near signal maximum. Required events to reject isotropy reduced by nearly 5x for 100 GeV DM in a CYGNUS-like experiment.
AI.conclusion: The LMC is crucial for interpreting and optimizing future directional DM searches, as it significantly enhances directional discovery prospects, especially for heavier DM particles.

title: Polarization Formalism for Photon-Gravitational Wave Mixing Around Magnetars
summary: The Gertsenshtein effect can be used to probe the stochastic gravitational wave background at high frequencies, well above the range of standard cosmological sources. In this paper, we revisit the conversion between electromagnetic and gravitational waves in the magnetosphere of magnetars by solving the evolution equations of the associated Stokes parameters. In the process, we point out that the adiabatic approximation usually taken in the literature is not generally justified in the context of the Gertsenshtein effect. To derive analytical results, we focus our attention on two specific geometries where the adiabatic approximation is valid. From these, we derive a lower bound on the stochastic gravitational wave background from the conversion of magnetar electromagnetic emission into gravitational waves, and an upper bound by requiring that the conversion of background gravitational waves into electromagnetic radiation does not exceed the observed magnetar flux in the X-ray band. Our results demonstrate that gravitational waves generated through the Gertsenshtein conversion of magnetar electromagnetic emission produce a negligible stochastic background, as anticipated.

AI.tldr: This paper reexamines the Gertsenshtein effect in magnetar magnetospheres for probing high-frequency gravitational waves, using Stokes parameter evolution equations. It finds that the adiabatic approximation commonly used is not generally valid, derives analytical results for two valid geometries, and establishes both lower and upper bounds on the stochastic gravitational wave background from magnetar electromagnetic conversion, concluding that magnetar-generated gravitational waves produce a negligible stochastic background.
AI.motivation: To probe the stochastic gravitational wave background at high frequencies beyond the range of standard cosmological sources using the Gertsenshtein effect in magnetar magnetospheres, and to address whether the commonly used adiabatic approximation is justified in this context.
AI.method: The authors solve evolution equations of Stokes parameters for electromagnetic-gravitational wave conversion in magnetar magnetospheres. They identify when the adiabatic approximation is valid, focus on two specific valid geometries for analytical results, and derive bounds by balancing conversion from magnetar emission (lower bound) and from background gravitational waves into X-ray flux (upper bound).
AI.result: The adiabatic approximation is not generally justified for the Gertsenshtein effect. In the two valid geometries analyzed, gravitational waves from magnetar electromagnetic emission produce a negligible stochastic background. Upper and lower bounds on the stochastic gravitational wave background are derived from observational constraints.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational waves generated via Gertsenshtein conversion of magnetar electromagnetic emission contribute negligibly to the stochastic background, confirming prior expectations, while the methodology provides a more rigorous framework for analyzing this effect.

title: Infinite-Order Lattice Chiral Anomalies and CPT
summary: A key property of a global symmetry's anomaly is its order: the smallest integer $n$ for which the diagonal symmetry of the $n$-copy system is anomaly-free. While many familiar lattice anomalies have finite order, perturbative anomalies in the continuum$-$those captured by Feynman diagrams$-$have infinite order. In this paper, we show that the Onsager symmetry, a lattice realization of the chiral symmetry of a 1+1d massless Dirac fermion, has an order-two anomaly. However, imposing lattice CPT symmetry enhances this anomaly from order two to infinite order, yielding a lattice chiral symmetry structure that more faithfully matches the continuum chiral anomaly. We also discuss the corresponding 2+1d symmetry-protected topological phases for these infinite-order lattice anomalies.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that the Onsager symmetry (lattice realization of 1+1d Dirac chiral symmetry) has an order-two anomaly, but imposing lattice CPT symmetry enhances it to infinite order, better matching the continuum chiral anomaly, with discussion of corresponding 2+1d SPT phases.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the finite-order anomalies observed in lattice systems with the infinite-order nature of perturbative (continuum) anomalies, using the chiral anomaly of a 1+1d massless Dirac fermion as a case study.
AI.method: Analysis of the Onsager symmetry on the lattice, demonstration of anomaly order-two without CPT, and enhancement to infinite order upon imposing lattice CPT symmetry; discussion of 2+1d symmetry-protected topological phases.
AI.result: Onsager symmetry has an order-two anomaly; imposing lattice CPT raises this to infinite order, faithfully reproducing the continuum chiral anomaly structure.
AI.conclusion: Lattice symmetries can exhibit infinite-order anomalies when CPT is imposed, bridging the gap between lattice and continuum anomaly structures, with implications for corresponding SPT phases.

title: Are Primordial Black Holes a Natural Dark Matter Candidate?
comment: 33 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables; comments very welcome!
summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) in the asteroid-mass window ($10^{17}$-$10^{22}$ g) can account for all of the dark matter without violating any observational constraint, yet are routinely dismissed as fine-tuned. I put that dismissal to the test by applying three complementary fine-tuning measures uniformly across a broad landscape: three non-inflationary PBH production mechanisms, six classes of inflationary PBH models, and seven particle dark matter benchmarks, all evaluated against the same observable target. Three distinct naturalness universality classes emerge, determined entirely by the analytic structure of the abundance map rather than by the nature of the dark matter candidate. Biased-domain-wall PBHs are as natural as off-resonance weakly interacting massive particles and freeze-in particles; early-matter-domination and first-order phase transition PBH mechanisms occupy an intermediate tier alongside coannihilating WIMPs, unified by a structural identity in which the fine-tuning measure equals the logarithm of the ratio of the formation scale to the matter-radiation equality scale; and single-field ultra-slow-roll inflationary collapse is severely tuned for a distinct reason: a double exponential in which the power spectrum amplitude is itself exponentially sensitive to the inflaton potential coefficients, on top of the exponential collapse sensitivity of the abundance map. My main conclusion is that {\em the claim that PBH dark matter is generically fine-tuned conflates the worst case with a landscape spanning every naturalness tier}. The three-measure protocol also resolves a tension in the recent literature: the Barbieri-Giudice and Iovino-Riotto fine-tuning measures answer complementary questions and are reconciled within the two-layer decomposition developed here.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically evaluates fine-tuning claims against primordial black hole (PBH) dark matter across three non-inflationary and six inflationary PBH production mechanisms, plus seven particle dark matter benchmarks, using three complementary fine-tuning measures. It identifies three naturalness universality classes determined by the abundance map's analytic structure, shows that biased-domain-wall PBHs are as natural as WIMPs and freeze-in particles, and concludes that claims of PBH dark matter being generically fine-tuned conflate the worst case with a diverse landscape.
AI.motivation: To test the widespread dismissal that PBH dark matter in the asteroid-mass window ($10^{17}$-$10^{22}$ g) is fine-tuned, by applying uniform fine-tuning measures across a broad landscape of PBH production mechanisms and comparing to particle dark matter benchmarks.
AI.method: Three complementary fine-tuning measures (including Barbieri-Giudice and Iovino-Riotto) applied uniformly across three non-inflationary PBH mechanisms, six classes of inflationary PBH models, and seven particle dark matter benchmarks, evaluated against the same observable target. A two-layer decomposition resolves tensions between different measures.
AI.result: Three naturalness universality classes emerge: (1) Biased-domain-wall PBHs are as natural as off-resonance WIMPs and freeze-in particles; (2) Early-matter-domination and first-order phase transition PBHs occupy an intermediate tier alongside coannihilating WIMPs, with fine-tuning measure = log(formation scale / matter-radiation equality scale); (3) Single-field ultra-slow-roll inflation is severely tuned due to a double exponential sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The claim that PBH dark matter is generically fine-tuned conflates the worst case (ultra-slow-roll inflation) with a landscape spanning every naturalness tier. The three-measure protocol resolves tensions between Barbieri-Giudice and Iovino-Riotto measures within a two-layer decomposition.

title: Localization of Chiral Electromagnetic Waves on Thick Axion Domain Walls
summary: We analyze Maxwell theory coupled to an axion domain wall as a spectral boundary value problem. We find that a finite-width axion domain wall generically supports a localized normalizable chiral electromagnetic mode with linear, gapless dispersion. This mode arises from helicity-dependent coupling sourced by the axion gradient: one polarization experiences an effective attractive potential and forms a bound state, while the opposite polarization is repelled. The existence of this chiral surface photon is robust over a wide regime of wall structures and axion masses. Our result shows that axion domain walls generically support a localized chiral photon that has been missed in previous analyses.

AI.tldr: Analyzing Maxwell theory with an axion domain wall reveals a localized, normalizable chiral electromagnetic mode with linear, gapless dispersion, arising from helicity-dependent coupling. This robust chiral surface photon was previously missed.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether axion domain walls support localized electromagnetic modes that may have been overlooked in prior studies.
AI.method: Analyzed Maxwell theory coupled to an axion domain wall as a spectral boundary value problem, examining finite-width wall structures and various axion masses.
AI.result: A finite-width axion domain wall generically supports a localized normalizable chiral electromagnetic mode with linear, gapless dispersion. One polarization is attracted and forms a bound state; the opposite is repelled.
AI.conclusion: Axion domain walls generically host a robust, localized chiral surface photon that was missed in previous analyses.

title: A simple solution to the monopole problem: SU(5) GUT with symmetry breaking into special subgroup
summary: Grand unified theories (GUTs) predict the overproduction of magnetic monopoles, leading to the so-called monopole problem, which is often addressed by cosmological inflation that dilutes their abundance. However, if inflation occurs before the GUT symmetry breaking, monopoles are produced afterwards and the problem persists. This motivates the exploration of alternative mechanisms. We propose a simple solution based on the Langacker--Pi mechanism within an $SU(5)$ GUT framework with symmetry breaking into its special subgroup. In particular, after the gauge symmetry is broken to the Standard Model (SM) gauge group $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ by the vacuum expectation value of an adjoint scalar, it is further broken to $SO(3)_C\times SO(2)_L$. This structure is naturally realized by introducing a symmetric tensor scalar, a singlet scalar, and multiple singlet fermions. During this intermediate phase, the monopoles become connected to antimonopoles by cosmic strings, which enhances their pair annihilation and reduces their abundance. Subsequently, the symmetry is restored to the SM gauge group. The restoration transition can be either first-order or second-order, depending on the model parameters. In the case of a first-order phase transition, a stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signal is generated. For a certain region of the parameter space, the resulting signal can lie within the sensitivity of future GW experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a solution to the GUT magnetic monopole problem using the Langacker-Pi mechanism within an SU(5) framework, where an intermediate symmetry breaking phase connects monopoles to antimonopoles via cosmic strings, enhancing annihilation. The subsequent symmetry restoration can produce detectable stochastic gravitational wave signals.
AI.motivation: The monopole problem persists in GUTs even after inflation if inflation occurs before GUT symmetry breaking. This motivates exploring alternative mechanisms beyond inflation to address monopole overproduction.
AI.method: The authors employ the Langacker-Pi mechanism within an SU(5) GUT framework, where symmetry breaks through an intermediate phase (SO(3)_C × SO(2)_L) via an adjoint scalar, symmetric tensor scalar, singlet scalar, and singlet fermions. Monopoles are connected by cosmic strings during this phase, enhancing pair annihilation.
AI.result: The intermediate phase enhances monopole-antimonopole annihilation, reducing their abundance. The restoration to the SM gauge group can be first- or second-order; a first-order transition generates stochastic GW signals potentially detectable by future experiments.
AI.conclusion: The Langacker-Pi mechanism offers a viable alternative to inflation for solving the monopole problem, with the added feature of testable GW signatures in certain parameter regions.

title: Mapping the Infrared Phase Space of Gravity to Finite Subregions
summary: We construct the phase space for an arbitrary cut of a null hypersurface in Minkowski spacetime and demonstrate that it is symplectomorphic to the infrared phase space of asymptotically flat gravity. Fluctuations of the cut are mapped to the leading soft graviton mode. Furthermore, the supertranslation Goldstone mode is mapped to the product of the size of the cut with its symplectic partner, the null time offset.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the phase space of arbitrary cuts on a null hypersurface in Minkowski spacetime is symplectomorphic to the infrared phase space of asymptotically flat gravity. Cut fluctuations map to the leading soft graviton mode, and the supertranslation Goldstone mode maps to cut size times null time offset.
AI.motivation: To establish a direct relationship between null hypersurface cuts in flat spacetime and the infrared structure of asymptotically flat gravity, bridging local geometric features with soft graviton degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Constructs the phase space for an arbitrary cut of a null hypersurface in Minkowski spacetime and demonstrates a symplectomorphism to the infrared phase space of asymptotically flat gravity.
AI.result: Fluctuations of the cut map to the leading soft graviton mode; the supertranslation Goldstone mode maps to the product of cut size and null time offset.
AI.conclusion: The infrared phase space of asymptotic gravity can be realized locally on a null hypersurface cut, providing a geometric interpretation of soft graviton and supertranslation Goldstone modes.

title: Mass Varying Neutrino Oscillation in Teleparallel Gravity
summary: In the Cartan teleparallel formulation of gravity, a scalar field coupled to the torsion tensor can acquire an environment dependent effective mass. This gives rise to a screening effect: Inside dense bodies such as the Sun, the scalar field is suppressed, causing the mass varying neutrino mass to vary with local density. We investigate the impact of this torsion-induced screening on solar neutrino oscillations. The mechanism modifies the standard MSW resonance condition in a distinct way, leading to detectable shift in the flavor conversion probability. Using data from solar neutrino experiments (Super-Kamiokande, Borexino, SNO), we place constraints on the torsion-scalar coupling parameters. Our work provides concrete test of teleparallel gravity through mass varying neutrino oscillations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a scalar field coupled to torsion in teleparallel gravity can screen neutrino masses in dense environments (like the Sun), altering MSW resonance and solar neutrino oscillations, and uses experimental data to constrain torsion-scalar coupling parameters.
AI.motivation: To test teleparallel gravity through observable effects on solar neutrino oscillations, by exploiting the density-dependent screening of scalar fields coupled to torsion, which modifies neutrino mass and flavor conversion.
AI.method: A scalar field coupled to torsion in Cartan teleparallel gravity acquires environment-dependent effective mass, causing screening. This induces mass-varying neutrino masses that depend on local density. The modified MSW resonance condition alters solar neutrino flavor conversion probabilities. Constraints are derived from Super-Kamiokande, Borexino, and SNO data.
AI.result: The torsion-induced screening modifies the standard MSW resonance condition, leading to detectable shifts in flavor conversion probability. Observational data place constraints on torsion-scalar coupling parameters.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a concrete test of teleparallel gravity via mass-varying neutrino oscillations, demonstrating that solar neutrino experiments can constrain torsion-scalar couplings.

title: Multi-entropy in heavy local quenches
summary: We study the time evolution of tripartite entanglement in heavy local quenches in two-dimensional holographic conformal field theories. Our diagnostic is the genuine multi-entropy of adjacent intervals, computed from both bulk and boundary perspectives. A perturbative bulk analysis shows that the first-order small-mass perturbation around the vacuum geodesic network cancels identically at any time after the quench. In the fully back-reacted geometry, a vacuum-subtracted genuine multi-entropy arises from a mismatch between the winding selected by the trivalent geodesic network and the windings selected independently by the pairwise geodesics. In the sharp quench limit, the time dependence of genuine multi-entropy is kinematically fixed to logarithms of rational functions of time and is independent of the heavy operator dimension. The CFT calculation reproduces the same formula within the heavy-light vacuum block approximation, where the branch choice in the heavy-background uniformization map corresponds to the winding selection in the bulk. These results indicate that, in this setup, the genuine multi-entropy is controlled by global saddle selection, rather than by a local energy response or quasiparticle propagation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies tripartite entanglement evolution after heavy local quenches in 2D holographic CFTs using genuine multi-entropy, finding it is governed by global saddle selection rather than local dynamics, with time dependence given by logarithms of rational functions independent of operator dimension.
AI.motivation: To understand how tripartite entanglement evolves in heavy local quenches in holographic CFTs, using genuine multi-entropy as a diagnostic to go beyond bipartite measures.
AI.method: Perturbative bulk analysis around vacuum geodesic network, fully back-reacted geometry computation, and CFT calculation using heavy-light vacuum block approximation with uniformization map.
AI.result: First-order small-mass perturbation cancels identically at any time. Vacuum-subtracted genuine multi-entropy arises from winding mismatch between trivalent and pairwise geodesic networks. Time dependence is kinematically fixed to logarithms of rational functions, independent of heavy operator dimension in the sharp quench limit.
AI.conclusion: Genuine multi-entropy is controlled by global saddle selection rather than local energy response or quasiparticle propagation in this holographic setup.

title: Nucleon matrix elements of axial anomaly, axial currents and pseudoscalar currents in the QCD sum rule
summary: We have analyzed one-nucleon matrix elements of current-current correlators; the currents consist of pseudoscalar octet, isovector and isoscalar currents, axial anomaly, and axial isovector and isoscalar currents. Using QCD sum rules, the coupling constants of nucleon with each of these currents have been expressed in terms of nucleon matrix elements of quark, gluon and quark-gluon composite operators and moments of parton distribution function. On the phenomenological side, contribution from the non-diagonal matrix elements of operators between nucleon and its excited states or continuum states have also been accounted for. For the pseudoscalar coupling constants of the nucleon two expressions have been obtained in which one of them consists of only moments of parton distribution function but yielding approximately same numerical result as the other one. Of particular interest is the nucleon matrix element of axial anomaly which has been largely ignored in the current literature.

AI.tldr: The paper uses QCD sum rules to analyze one-nucleon matrix elements of current-current correlators (pseudoscalar, isovector, isoscalar, axial anomaly, axial currents), expressing nucleon coupling constants in terms of parton distribution moments and composite operator matrix elements, with special attention to the previously neglected axial anomaly contribution.
AI.motivation: To systematically analyze one-nucleon matrix elements of various current-current correlators using QCD sum rules, with particular focus on the nucleon matrix element of the axial anomaly which has been largely ignored in existing literature.
AI.method: QCD sum rules applied to current-current correlators involving pseudoscalar octet, isovector/isoscalar currents, axial anomaly, and axial isovector/isoscalar currents. Coupling constants expressed in terms of nucleon matrix elements of quark, gluon, and quark-gluon composite operators, and moments of parton distribution functions. Non-diagonal matrix elements between nucleon and excited/continuum states included.
AI.result: Two expressions derived for pseudoscalar coupling constants of the nucleon — one using only moments of parton distribution functions, yielding numerically similar results to the other. The axial anomaly matrix element, previously neglected, is analyzed in detail.
AI.conclusion: The analysis provides a systematic QCD sum rule framework for nucleon coupling constants with various currents, accounting for non-diagonal contributions and highlighting the importance of the axial anomaly matrix element.

title: How traversable is a traversable wormhole?
summary: To answer the above question, we study low-frequency scattering in the four-dimensional traversable wormhole of Maldacena, Milekhin, and Popov. The resulting transmission probabilities reveal that wormhole traversability depends strongly on the nature of the probe. For scalar probes, both neutral and charged, traversability depends on the time scale. On time scales of order the light-crossing time after sending in a signal, the transmission is parametrically suppressed, with most of the incoming signal reflected or temporarily trapped inside the wormhole throat. As time progresses, the trapped signal gradually leaks out, so that at late times the accumulated transmission cross-section approaches one half of the corresponding black hole absorption cross-section. Despite this generic suppression at low frequencies, the transmission spectrum also exhibits resonant frequencies at which transmission becomes perfect. Charged massless fermions tell a very different story. Unlike scalars, they traverse the wormhole with essentially unit probability at low energies. The same mechanism underlies their efficient absorption by magnetic black holes and realizes a channel closely analogous to the Callan-Rubakov effect, revealing unexpected connections with monopole-fermion scattering. Putting everything together, we conclude that scalar probes are best suited for uncovering distinct features of these magnetic wormholes, while charged massless fermions are the ideal carriers of information through them.

AI.tldr: This paper studies low-frequency scattering in a four-dimensional traversable wormhole, finding that scalar probes experience suppressed transmission with resonant peaks, while charged massless fermions traverse with near-unit probability, similar to the Callan-Rubakov effect.
AI.motivation: To understand how traversability of the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov wormhole depends on the nature of the probing field, particularly comparing scalar and fermionic probes.
AI.method: Analytical study of low-frequency scattering in the four-dimensional traversable wormhole background of Maldacena, Milekhin, and Popov, computing transmission probabilities for scalar (neutral and charged) and charged massless fermion probes.
AI.result: Scalar transmission is parametrically suppressed at early times but accumulates to half the black hole absorption cross-section at late times, with resonant perfect transmission frequencies. Charged massless fermions traverse with near-unit probability at low energies, analogous to the Callan-Rubakov effect in monopole-fermion scattering.
AI.conclusion: Scalar probes are best for revealing distinct wormhole features, while charged massless fermions are ideal information carriers through the wormhole.

title: A generalised-$k_t$ jet algorithm for Deep Inelastic Scattering
comment: 22 pages. Code available through fjcontrib at https://repo.hepforge.org/source/fastjetsvn/browse/contrib/contribs/DISGenkt
summary: We introduce an inclusive generalised-$k_t$ jet algorithm for Deep Inelastic Scattering, defined in the Breit frame and implemented in fjcontrib. The family of algorithms is governed by the usual parameter $p$, which controls the transverse-momentum dependence of the algorithm, as well as by a jet radius parameter $R$. The angular-ordered ($p=0$) version of the algorithm was already presented by some of us, and can be used to formulate observables with simple all-order structures. In this article we investigate phenomenological applications of the algorithms related to the identification of the jet associated with the struck quark, and assess their sensitivity to non-perturbative effects, such as hadronisation. We also perform comparisons with the recent Centauro algorithm.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an inclusive generalised-$k_t$ jet algorithm for Deep Inelastic Scattering in the Breit frame, implemented in fjcontrib, governed by parameters $p$ and $R$. It studies phenomenological applications for identifying the struck quark jet and evaluates sensitivity to non-perturbative effects, with comparisons to the Centauro algorithm.
AI.motivation: To extend jet algorithms suitable for Deep Inelastic Scattering in the Breit frame, enabling the formulation of observables with simple all-order structures and practical identification of the struck quark jet.
AI.method: Generalised-$k_t$ jet algorithm family in the Breit frame with parameters $p$ (controlling transverse-momentum dependence) and $R$ (jet radius), implemented in fjcontrib; phenomenological studies and comparisons with the Centauro algorithm.
AI.result: The angular-ordered ($p=0$) version enables observables with simple all-order structures; the algorithms show varying sensitivity to hadronisation and non-perturbative effects; comparisons with Centauro algorithm are provided.
AI.conclusion: The generalised-$k_t$ algorithms are effective for struck quark jet identification in DIS, with the $p=0$ version particularly suited for all-order resummation studies.

title: Analytic approaches to perturbations of strongly coupled Yang-Mills plasma
summary: We study perturbations of Yang-Mills plasma, represented by scalar quasinormal modes of AdS black branes, as functions of the wave number $q$ in the entire range from zero to infinity. At finite $q$, these modes can be computed by classical spectral methods based on truncating the boundary value problem. We show that this truncation admits a natural analytic interpretation in terms of quantum Seiberg--Witten periods in the Nekrasov--Shatashvili limit, with the spectral condition organised as an instanton expansion around small values of the counting parameter. The physical black-brane problem corresponds to evaluating this series at a finite value of the counting parameter, and the Seiberg--Witten formulation provides a systematic way to analyse when the truncation is under control. In particular, it reveals that, as $q$ or the mode number $N$ increases, the physical point approaches the boundary of the domain of convergence of the instanton expansion, limiting the validity of the truncation approach. We overcome this limitation through an exact WKB analysis in which $q^{-1}$ acts as the expansion parameter. The resulting exact quantisation conditions, expressed in terms of period integrals and the associated Stokes geometry, incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative corrections. The resummed quasinormal modes remain accurate far beyond the strict large-$q$ regime and can be analytically continued all the way to $q=0$, notably by using the Seiberg--Witten approach, providing a consistent description of the QNM spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper bridges Yang-Mills plasma quasinormal modes (scalar QNMs of AdS black branes) with Seiberg-Witten theory and exact WKB analysis, showing that classical spectral truncation maps to an instanton expansion whose convergence domain limits the approach, and overcoming this via exact WKB with $q^{-1}$ as expansion parameter, achieving analytic continuation to $q=0$ via Seiberg-Witten periods.
AI.motivation: To understand perturbations of Yang-Mills plasma across all wave numbers $q$, overcoming limitations of classical truncation methods for computing quasinormal modes of AdS black branes.
AI.method: (1) Classical spectral truncation mapped to Seiberg-Witten periods in Nekrasov-Shatashvili limit, organized as instanton expansion; (2) Exact WKB analysis with $q^{-1}$ as expansion parameter, using period integrals and Stokes geometry for exact quantization conditions.
AI.result: The truncation approach fails when $q$ or mode number $N$ increases as the physical point approaches the convergence boundary of the instanton expansion. The exact WKB method yields resummed QNMs accurate beyond the large-$q$ regime, analytically continuable to $q=0$ via Seiberg-Witten.
AI.conclusion: The Seiberg-Witten formulation diagnoses truncation validity, and exact WKB combined with Seiberg-Witten provides a consistent, non-perturbative description of the full QNM spectrum across all $q$.

title: Mass spectra and electromagnetic characteristics of the $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}{D}^{(*)}$ molecular tetraquarks from the coupled-channel dynamics
summary: Motivated by the observation of numerous charmed-strange hadrons lying close to the $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ thresholds, we systematically investigate their mass spectra and electromagnetic characteristics, explicitly incorporating the $S$-$D$ wave mixing and coupled-channel effects. For the mass spectra, we employ the one-boson-exchange model and obtain several promising $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular candidates awaiting future experimental confirmation. The coupled-channel dynamics is found to play an essential role: it not only enhances binding in existing channels but also generates new loosely bound states that are absent in the single-channel approximation. Regarding the electromagnetic characteristics, we discuss the M1 radiative decay widths and magnetic moments of these charmed-strange molecular tetraquarks based on our obtained mass spectra and spatial wave functions within the constituent quark model. Our results demonstrate that the electromagnetic observables serve as valuable discriminants for clarifying the nature of these hadronic molecules. We encourage experimental collaborations to focus on such predicted charmed-strange molecular tetraquark candidates, especially the genuinely exotic $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ states comprising four different flavors with valence quark content $\bar c \bar s u d$.

title: Higher Gauge Theory via Differential Nonabelian Cohomology
summary: This is a streamlined introduction to the global (infrared) completion of Maxwell-type higher gauge fields (as in the higher gauge sectors of higher dimensional supergravity and its brane probes) by electromagnetic flux quantization in differential nonabelian cohomology, using cohesive homotopy theory. Applications include D/NS brane charge in (unstable) K-theory, M-brane charge in unstable Cohomotopy and geometric engineering of topological quantum order on probe M5-branes.

Applications include D/NS brane charge in (unstable) K-theory, M-brane charge in unstable Cohomotopy, and topological quantum order on probe M5-branes.
AI.motivation: To provide a systematic framework for understanding the global (infrared) completion of higher gauge fields that appear in higher-dimensional supergravity and brane probes, particularly addressing flux quantization beyond the abelian case.
AI.method: Uses cohesive homotopy theory to formulate electromagnetic flux quantization in differential nonabelian cohomology, enabling the global completion of Maxwell-type higher gauge fields.
AI.result: Establishes a unified mathematical framework that captures D/NS brane charge in unstable K-theory, M-brane charge in unstable Cohomotopy, and enables geometric engineering of topological quantum order on probe M5-branes.
AI.conclusion: Differential nonabelian cohomology via cohesive homotopy theory provides a powerful tool for completing higher gauge theories globally, with concrete applications to brane charge quantization and topological quantum matter.

title: Correlation Between Proton Decay Channels and the Axion Mass in an Extended SU(5) GUT
summary: We study a renormalizable SU(5) grand unified theory (GUT) supplemented by a 45-dimensional Higgs field and a DFSZ axion sector, imposing a Georgi--Jarlskog flavor structure at the unification scale. We perform a one-loop gauge coupling unification analysis, explicitly including the threshold masses of the light multiplets arising from the 45-dimensional Higgs field. This analysis identifies the viable region in the $(M_{\mathrm{GUT}},M_{S_1})$ parameter space. Through the relation between the unification and PQ scales, this region yields correlated predictions for the QCD axion mass. The Georgi--Jarlskog assumption substantially reduces the flavor ambiguity of the dimension-six baryon-violating operators, enabling robust constraints and predictions not only for antineutrino modes but also for charged-lepton proton decay modes such as $p \to e^+ π^0$. We present the combined implications for proton decay and axion searches, showing how the GUT-selected parameter region maps onto the axion mass, the axion-photon coupling, and the axion-induced EDM coupling.

AI.tldr: This paper studies an SU(5) GUT with a 45-dimensional Higgs and DFSZ axion sector, using Georgi-Jarlskog flavor structure. It performs one-loop gauge coupling unification, identifies viable (M_GUT, M_S1) parameter space, and predicts correlated QCD axion mass. The flavor structure reduces uncertainty in dimension-six proton decay operators, enabling robust predictions for p → e⁺π⁰ and other modes. Combined constraints on axion mass, axion-photon coupling, and axion-induced EDM coupling are presented.
AI.motivation: To explore a renormalizable SU(5) GUT with a 45-dimensional Higgs and DFSZ axion sector, imposing Georgi-Jarlskog flavor structure, and to derive correlated predictions for proton decay and axion observables by reducing flavor uncertainties in baryon-violating operators.
AI.method: One-loop gauge coupling unification analysis including threshold masses from the 45-dimensional Higgs multiplets; scanning the (M_GUT, M_S1) parameter space; using Georgi-Jarlskog ansatz to constrain dimension-six baryon-violating operators; mapping the GUT-selected region onto axion mass, axion-photon coupling, and axion-induced EDM coupling.
AI.result: Identified viable region in (M_GUT, M_S1) parameter space from gauge coupling unification; derived correlated predictions for QCD axion mass via the unification-PQ scale relation; obtained robust constraints on both antineutrino and charged-lepton proton decay modes (e.g., p → e⁺π⁰); presented combined implications for axion mass, axion-photon coupling, and axion-induced EDM coupling.

The predicted axion mass and couplings are correlated with unification scale parameters, offering testable predictions for future experiments.

title: Wigner continuous-spin equations in $\mathbf{AdS_D}$: bosonic and fermionic cases
summary: We construct Wigner-like equations of motion for symmetric continuous-spin fields in anti-de Sitter space of arbitrary dimension, treating both the bosonic and fermionic cases. We generalise the classical flat-space Wigner constraints for bosonic continuous-spin fields, and for the fermionic case we adopt the equations proposed by Bekaert and Mourad as our starting point. This is achieved by covariantising the ordinary derivatives and deforming the resulting constraints so that they form a closed algebra. The construction is carried out in a metric-like formalism and yields a system of first-class constraints that define a representation of the $\mathfrak{so}(2,D-1)$ isometry algebra, realised via the Lie-Lorentz derivative. Using these constraints, we compute the eigenvalues of the quadratic and quartic Casimir operators and compare the obtained values with Metsaev's classification of continuous-spin representations for both the bosonic and fermionic cases. A crucial algebraic role is played by special operators of the (super)algebra Howe-dual to the Lorentz subalgebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,D-1)$: the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ Casimir operator in the bosonic case, and the Casimir's ghost of the $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ superalgebra in the fermionic case. Both objects naturally organise the constraint algebra and ensure its consistency.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Wigner-like equations of motion for symmetric continuous-spin fields in anti-de Sitter space (AdS) for both bosonic and fermionic cases, using a metric-like formalism with first-class constraints that realize the so(2,D-1) isometry algebra and compute Casimir eigenvalues consistent with Metsaev's classification.
AI.motivation: To extend the description of continuous-spin fields from flat space to anti-de Sitter space for both bosonic and fermionic cases, generalizing Wigner's equations and Bekaert-Mourad's proposals.
AI.method: Covariantizing ordinary derivatives and deforming constraints to form a closed algebra in a metric-like formalism; using Lie-Lorentz derivatives to realize the so(2,D-1) isometry algebra; employing sl(2) Casimir (bosonic) and osp(1|2) Casimir ghost (fermionic) operators from the Howe-dual algebra to organize the constraint algebra.
AI.result: Derived a system of first-class constraints defining a representation of so(2,D-1); computed quadratic and quartic Casimir eigenvalues; verified consistency with Metsaev's classification of continuous-spin representations for both bosonic and fermionic cases.
AI.conclusion: The construction successfully generalizes continuous-spin field equations to AdS space, with the Howe-dual sl(2) and osp(1|2) algebras playing a crucial algebraic role in ensuring constraint algebra consistency and matching the known representation theory classification.

title: Electroweak precision physics via angular distributions in hadronic $τ$ decays
summary: Hadronic tau decays provide a unique low-energy laboratory for the charged-current interaction between quarks and leptons. Their use as an electroweak precision sector is, however, limited by nonperturbative QCD dynamics in the resonance region, encoded in hadronic form factors. In this work we show that angular information in two-hadron tau decays can be used to construct observables in which these form factors cancel, leading to first-principles Standard Model predictions up to light-quark-mass and radiative corrections. We derive the fully differential distributions for arbitrary two-pseudoscalar final states, including tau polarization, and extend them to the Weak Effective Field Theory at linear order in new-physics couplings. We then illustrate our strategy with several benchmark observables, for both unpolarized and polarized taus, whose Standard Model predictions can be obtained without modelling the dominant hadronic form factors and which receive characteristic beyond-the-Standard-Model corrections, in particular from tensor currents. These results provide concrete targets for Belle II, polarized-tau proposals such as Chiral Belle, and future high-statistics facilities, including super-tau-charm factories and FCC-ee, to test the electroweak structure of hadronic tau decays.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that angular information in two-hadron tau decays can construct observables where hadronic form factors cancel, enabling first-principles Standard Model predictions up to quark-mass and radiative corrections. The authors derive differential distributions for two-pseudoscalar final states including tau polarization, extend to Weak Effective Field Theory, and illustrate benchmark observables that receive characteristic beyond-Standard-Model corrections, particularly from tensor currents.
AI.motivation: Hadronic tau decays are a valuable probe of charged-current interactions, but their electroweak precision utility is limited by nonperturbative QCD dynamics encoded in hadronic form factors. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by constructing observables where these form factors cancel.
AI.method: The authors derive fully differential distributions for two-pseudoscalar tau decays including polarization effects, extend the formalism to Weak Effective Field Theory at linear order in new-physics couplings, and construct benchmark observables where the dominant hadronic form factors cancel.
AI.result: Several benchmark observables (for both unpolarized and polarized taus) are identified for which Standard Model predictions can be obtained without modeling the dominant hadronic form factors, and which receive characteristic beyond-Standard-Model corrections, especially from tensor currents.
AI.conclusion: These observables provide concrete targets for Belle II, Chiral Belle, super-tau-charm factories, and FCC-ee to test the electroweak structure of hadronic tau decays with reduced hadronic uncertainties.

title: Toward Entanglement Bootstrap for Conformal Field Theory in Any Dimension
summary: Given a quantum critical wavefunction in any dimension, we propose a reconstructed Hamiltonian, analogous to the ones previously found for 1+1d CFT and for 2+1d bosonic liquid topologically-ordered states. We test numerically that, for known regularized approximate CFT groundstates (on the icosahedron and the fuzzy sphere), (1) they are close to the groundstate of their reconstructed Hamiltonian, and (2) the spectrum of their reconstructed Hamiltonian on the unit sphere has CFT properties (integer spacing of descendants) and matches known low-lying energies. We show that this provides an automated method to improve the finite-size effects in a fixed Hilbert space.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a reconstructed Hamiltonian for quantum critical wavefunctions in any dimension, tests it on approximate CFT groundstates (icosahedron and fuzzy sphere), and shows it improves finite-size effects and yields CFT-like spectra.
AI.motivation: To extend the concept of a reconstructed Hamiltonian — previously known for 1+1d CFT and 2+1d topologically-ordered states — to quantum critical wavefunctions in arbitrary dimensions, enabling improved finite-size analysis and extraction of CFT data.
AI.method: The authors propose a general reconstruction procedure for Hamiltonians from a given quantum critical wavefunction. They numerically test it on regularized approximate CFT groundstates on the icosahedron and fuzzy sphere by checking groundstate overlap and comparing the reconstructed Hamiltoian's spectrum (on the unit sphere) against expected CFT properties (integer descendant spacing and low-lying energies).
AI.result: (1) The approximate CFT groundstates are close to the groundstate of their reconstructed Hamiltonian. (2) The reconstructed Hamiltonian's spectrum on the unit sphere exhibits CFT properties (integer spacing of descendants) and matches known low-lying energies.
AI.conclusion: The reconstructed Hamiltonian provides an automated method to mitigate finite-size effects within a fixed Hilbert space, improving the extraction of conformal data from approximate quantum critical wavefunctions.

title: Resolving the CP Asymmetry Puzzle in $B$ Decays with Unitarized Final-State Interactions
summary: A reliable description of direct CP asymmetries in hadronic $B$ decays, among the most sensitive probes of the CKM mechanism and of physics beyond the Standard Model, remains unresolved. Conventional factorization approaches adopt distinct treatments for the strong phases originating from long-distance QCD interactions, leading to predictions that differ by factors of several for identical decay channels. Existing final-state interaction (FSI) models are limited to one-loop approximations that break unitarity and rely on channel-specific phenomenological cutoffs, severely restricting the predictive capability. We introduce a unitarized FSI framework based on the Lippmann-Schwinger equation solved to all orders, restoring unitarity that is manifestly broken in one-loop treatments. Using the coupled $D\bar{D}$ system, we show that the interaction kernel can be derived from chiral effective field theory constrained by heavy-quark spin symmetry, and low-energy constants are fixed by the $γγ\to D\bar{D}$ cross-section data from BaBar, leaving no adjustable parameter in the FSI sector when applied to $B$ decays. The resulting predictions for CP asymmetries and branching fractions show excellent agreement with the available experimental data. A defining consequence is that CP asymmetries in the pure-annihilation channels $\bar{B}^0\to D^0\bar{D}^0$ and $\bar{B}^0\to D_s^+D_s^-$, identically zero in any short-distance treatment, are dramatically enhanced by FSI, and a measured nonzero asymmetry in these modes is therefore a direct experimental signature of long-distance dynamics. We present definite predictions for the partial widths and CP asymmetries of all yet-unmeasured channels, establishing final-state interactions as a predictive, data-driven ingredient of the Standard Model with direct implications for CKM parameter extraction and BSM searches.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a unitarized final-state interaction (FSI) framework based on the Lippmann-Schwinger equation solved to all orders, restoring broken unitarity in one-loop treatments. Applied to hadronic B decays, it derives the interaction kernel from chiral effective field theory with heavy-quark spin symmetry, fixing low-energy constants using BaBar γγ→D̄D data with no adjustable FSI parameters. Predictions for CP asymmetries and branching fractions match experimental data well, notably enhancing CP asymmetries in pure-annihilation channels that are zero in short-distance approaches, establishing FSI as a predictive Standard Model ingredient for CKM extraction and BSM searches.
AI.motivation: Reliable description of direct CP asymmetries in hadronic B decays remains unresolved; conventional factorization approaches yield predictions differing by factors of several, and existing FSI models using one-loop approximations break unitarity and rely on channel-specific cutoffs, limiting predictive capability.
AI.method: Unitarized FSI framework using the Lippmann-Schwinger equation solved to all orders; interaction kernel derived from chiral effective field theory with heavy-quark spin symmetry; low-energy constants fixed by BaBar γγ→D̄D cross-section data, leaving no adjustable FSI parameters when applied to B decays.

CP asymmetries in pure-annihilation channels B̄^0→D^0D̄^0 and B̄^0→D_s^+D_s^- (identically zero in short-distance treatments) are dramatically enhanced by FSI. Definite predictions provided for all yet-unmeasured channels.
AI.conclusion: Final-state interactions are established as a predictive, data-driven ingredient of the Standard Model with direct implications for CKM parameter extraction and BSM searches. Nonzero asymmetry in pure-annihilation modes is a direct experimental signature of long-distance dynamics.

title: Vacuum photon emission and mean electromagnetic field in pair-creating external backgrounds
summary: We develop a perturbative description of vacuum radiative processes in quantum electrodynamics with a prescribed external electromagnetic background capable of producing electron-positron pairs. Since the initial vacuum is then unstable and the in- and out-vacua are inequivalent, radiative observables require a real-time formulation beyond the ordinary in-out approach of vacuum-stable QED. Using the Keldysh-Schwinger-Fradkin nonequilibrium technique, we derive the mean number density of emitted photons through the second nonvanishing order in the fine-structure constant. The leading term, of order $α$, reproduces the known vertex and tadpole mechanisms, while the complete order-$α^2$ correction contains interference, loop, and induced-current contributions. We also give an independent derivation based on the spectral decomposition of the identity operator in the in-Fock space, where the photon number density is represented as a sum of squared transition amplitudes and vacuum-disconnected terms are canceled by the optical theorem generalized to an unstable vacuum. In addition, we compute the mean electromagnetic field through order $e^3$, including the electromagnetic dressing of the induced vacuum current, and verify it using the corresponding Schwinger-Dyson equations. The final formulas are expressed in terms of exact solutions and propagators of the Dirac equation in the external background and apply to general spacetime-dependent field configurations.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a perturbative real-time framework for computing photon emission in QED with pair-producing external backgrounds, going beyond the standard in-out formalism. Using the Keldysh-Schwinger-Fradkin technique, they derive the mean photon number density up to order α², including interference, loop, and induced-current terms. They also provide an independent derivation via in-Fock space spectral decomposition and compute the mean electromagnetic field through order e³, with all results expressed in terms of exact Dirac solutions.
AI.motivation: Standard in-out QED formalism fails for unstable vacua where electron-positron pairs are produced by external backgrounds, necessitating a real-time treatment for radiative processes like photon emission.
AI.method: Keldysh-Schwinger-Fradkin nonequilibrium real-time technique; spectral decomposition of in-Fock space identity; generalized optical theorem for unstable vacuum; Schwinger-Dyson equations.
AI.result: Mean photon number density derived to order α² (vertex, tadpole, interference, loop, induced-current contributions); mean electromagnetic field to order e³ with vacuum current dressing; verification via Schwinger-Dyson equations.
AI.conclusion: The formalism provides a systematic perturbative approach for radiative observables in unstable vacua, expressed in terms of exact Dirac solutions and propagators, applicable to general spacetime-dependent backgrounds.

title: Exploring Exotic Spin-Dependent Interactions Beyond the Standard Model: Theoretical Foundations and Experimental Investigations
summary: New interactions mediated by novel particles propose solutions to several important questions in modern physics. Axions serve as examples of such particles; they are lightweight and interact weakly with ordinary matter. This category of particles, including those similar to axions-termed Axion-Like Particles (ALPs)-arises from diverse theoretical frameworks, such as the Peccei-Quinn mechanism addressing the strong CP problem, string theory, and spontaneous supersymmetry breaking. Given their light mass and weak coupling, ALPs are also possible candidates for cold dark matter. Introducing these new interactions mediated by novel particles not only tackles several challenges in modern physics but also raises a crucial question: Are there undiscovered interactions beyond the Standard Model? Many of the interactions predicted by these theories are spin-dependent, which is the primary focus of this review. In this review, we first outline the theoretical foundations for investigating exotic spin-dependent interactions, highlighting their importance in various models beyond the Standard Model. We examine the potential roles of new lightweight particles in mediating these interactions, which may enhance our understanding of dark matter. Relevant formulas derived from theoretical models are included to support experimental investigations. Following this theoretical framework, we conduct a detailed review of recent experimental efforts to detect these exotic interactions. A systematic review of current constraints on these interactions is presented, along with an assessment of various detection approaches.

AI.tldr: This review examines theoretical foundations and experimental efforts to detect exotic spin-dependent interactions mediated by axion-like particles (ALPs) beyond the Standard Model, including their role as cold dark matter candidates.
AI.motivation: New particles like axions and ALPs, arising from the Peccei-Quinn mechanism, string theory, and supersymmetry breaking, may solve fundamental problems in modern physics (strong CP problem, dark matter). The paper seeks to explore whether undiscovered spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model exist.
AI.method: The paper provides a theoretical foundation for exotic spin-dependent interactions, includes relevant formulas from theoretical models, and systematically reviews recent experimental efforts and detection approaches for these interactions.
AI.result: A systematic compilation of current experimental constraints on exotic spin-dependent interactions mediated by lightweight particles, along with an assessment of various detection methodologies.
AI.conclusion: Spin-dependent interactions mediated by ALPs represent a promising avenue for discovering physics beyond the Standard Model and understanding dark matter, with active experimental efforts placing increasingly stringent constraints.

title: Tachyonic Encore: A universal shift of inflationary observables
summary: We propose a generic, largely inflaton-potential-independent mechanism in which a light axion spectator, initialized near the hilltop of its potential, reshapes inflationary observables through purely gravitational multi-field dynamics. During inflation the axion is frozen and the background follows an effectively single-field trajectory. After inflation ends, the axion rolls, inducing a turn in field space and transient tachyonic phases of the isocurvature mode. The resulting ``tachyonic encore'' occurs entirely on super-horizon scales. These phases generate a nearly scale-invariant enhancement of the curvature power spectrum, suppressing the tensor-to-scalar ratio and shifting the scalar tilt to a weighted combination of adiabatic and entropic tilts at horizon crossing. We show that these effects can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with current CMB constraints. The same dynamics predict local non-Gaussianity, $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc.}\sim \mathcal{O}(1)$, within reach of upcoming surveys.

AI.tldr: A light axion spectator field, initialized near a hilltop, creates a "tachyonic encore" after inflation through gravitational multi-field dynamics, generating nearly scale-invariant enhancements to the curvature power spectrum that can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with CMB data, while predicting local non-Gaussianity of order unity.
AI.motivation: To develop a generic, inflaton-potential-independent mechanism that can reconcile disfavored inflaton potentials with current CMB constraints via multi-field gravitational dynamics involving a light axion spectator.
AI.method: The authors introduce a light axion spectator field initialized near the hilltop of its potential. During inflation the axion is frozen, yielding effectively single-field dynamics; after inflation ends, the axion rolls, causing a field-space turn and transient tachyonic isocurvature modes on super-horizon scales (the "tachyonic encore").
AI.result: The mechanism produces a nearly scale-invariant enhancement of the curvature power spectrum, suppresses the tensor-to-scalar ratio, and shifts the scalar tilt to a weighted combination of adiabatic and entropic tilts. This can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with CMB constraints, and predicts local non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc.}\sim \mathcal{O}(1)$.
AI.conclusion: The proposed axion spectator mechanism provides a generic way to modify inflationary observables post-inflation via purely gravitational multi-field effects, offering a testable signature ($\mathcal{O}(1)$ local non-Gaussianity) for upcoming surveys.

title: Probing damping effects in neutrino oscillations with the first JUNO data
summary: We consider different scenarios which lead to a damping of the neutrino oscillation probability and investigate their impact on the first JUNO results. First, we study decoherence effects due to wave packet separation. In addition, we consider an open quantum system framework and adopt a phenomenological approach which allows us to parameterize the energy dependence of the decoherence effects more freely. Finally, we study the effect of invisible neutrino decay. In all cases with the first data JUNO can already place competitive bounds on the parameter space of the scenarios under consideration, while also maintaining a robust measurement of the standard neutrino oscillation parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how different damping mechanisms (wave packet decoherence, open quantum system decoherence, and invisible neutrino decay) affect neutrino oscillation probabilities and evaluates JUNO's ability to constrain these scenarios with first data while maintaining standard parameter measurements.
AI.motivation: To explore various physical scenarios that cause damping of neutrino oscillation probabilities and assess their impact on the first results from the JUNO experiment.
AI.method: The authors study three scenarios: (1) decoherence from wave packet separation, (2) an open quantum system framework with flexible energy-dependent parameterization of decoherence, and (3) invisible neutrino decay. They analyze how these affect oscillation probabilities and JUNO's sensitivity.
AI.result: JUNO with first data can place competitive bounds on the parameter space of all three damping scenarios while still maintaining a robust measurement of standard neutrino oscillation parameters.
AI.conclusion: JUNO's early data will provide strong constraints on beyond-standard-model decoherence and decay scenarios, demonstrating the experiment's versatility beyond standard oscillation measurements.

title: The state/defect correspondence
comment: 31 pages, 2 figures, many defects, just as many states
summary: We formulate a one-to-one correspondence between states and defects for higher-form gauge theories in arbitrary dimensions. The correspondence is not predicated on conformal invariance, as these theories are in general not conformal. Instead, it relies on the existence of infinitely many conserved charges associated with the mixed anomaly of electric and magnetic higher-form symmetries. In $p$-form Maxwell theory, these charges generate an extended Kac-Moody algebra that acts simultaneously on states and on extended operators. We show that this algebra organizes the Hilbert space on $S^p \times S^{d-p-1}$ into highest-weight representations allowing for a direct identification between states and $p$-dimensional defects. In particular, Wilson-'t Hooft defects dressed with local gauge-invariant operators are mapped to squeezed energy eigenstates. We further relate these novel symmetries to higher-spin currents and demonstrate that their construction persists in a class of interacting non-linear electrodynamics theories.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a one-to-one correspondence between states and defects in higher-form gauge theories using infinitely many conserved charges from mixed anomalies, constructs an extended Kac-Moody algebra organizing the Hilbert space, and maps Wilson-'t Hooft defects dressed with local operators to squeezed energy eigenstates, with extensions to nonlinear electrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous correspondence between states and defects in higher-form gauge theories without relying on conformal invariance, using conserved charges from mixed anomalies of electric and magnetic higher-form symmetries.
AI.method: The paper constructs an extended Kac-Moody algebra from infinitely many conserved charges arising from the mixed anomaly between electric and magnetic higher-form symmetries, and uses it to organize the Hilbert space on $S^p \times S^{d-p-1}$ into highest-weight representations.
AI.result: Wilson-'t Hooft defects dressed with local gauge-invariant operators are shown to correspond to squeezed energy eigenstates. The symmetries are related to higher-spin currents and persist in a class of interacting nonlinear electrodynamics theories.
AI.conclusion: A direct, non-conformal identification between states and defects exists in higher-form gauge theories, governed by an infinite-dimensional symmetry algebra that extends beyond free Maxwell theory to certain interacting theories.

title: Transport coefficients of strongly interacting quark-gluon plasma including elastic and inelastic scattering within the dynamical quasiparticle model
summary: We study the impact of inelastic gluon-radiation processes on the transport coefficients of the quark-gluon plasma within the dynamical quasiparticle model (DQPM) in the temperature-baryon-chemical-potential plane $(T,μ_B)$. Extending the elastic baseline established in previous DQPM calculations, we include radiative $2\to3$ scattering channels with massive partons and effective DQPM propagators and vertices. The corresponding momentum-dependent interaction rates and relaxation times are used within the relaxation-time approximation to calculate the shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, electric conductivity, and baryon diffusion coefficient as functions of temperature $T$ and baryon chemical potential $μ_B$. We find that radiative channels systematically reduce all considered transport coefficients relative to the elastic-only results, in accordance with the decrease of the relaxation times. In the thermal regime explored here, however, this reduction remains moderate, since the inelastic rates stay below the elastic ones over the considered $(T,μ_B)$ range. The radiative channels become more relevant mainly for partonic scatterings at large momenta, which are thermally suppressed in the strongly interacting QGP. At $μ_B=0$, the resulting $η/s$, $ζ/s$, and $σ_Q/T$ are compatible with available lattice-QCD estimates within uncertainties. At finite $μ_B$, our results provide predictions for the transport properties of QCD matter relevant for beam-energy-scan programs.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how inelastic gluon-radiation processes affect transport coefficients of quark-gluon plasma within the DQPM framework across the (T, μ_B) plane. Including 2→3 scattering channels reduces all transport coefficients (shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, electric conductivity, baryon diffusion) moderately compared to elastic-only results. At μ_B=0, results agree with lattice QCD; at finite μ_B, predictions for beam-energy-scan programs are provided.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of inelastic gluon-radiation processes on the transport coefficients of quark-gluon plasma beyond elastic scattering approximations, especially for finite baryon chemical potential relevant to heavy-ion collision experiments.
AI.method: The DQPM framework extended from elastic baseline to include radiative 2→3 scattering channels with massive partons and effective DQPM propagators and vertices. Momentum-dependent interaction rates and relaxation times are computed within the relaxation-time approximation to calculate shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, electric conductivity, and baryon diffusion coefficient as functions of T and μ_B.
AI.result: All considered transport coefficients are systematically reduced relative to elastic-only results due to decreased relaxation times. The reduction remains moderate as inelastic rates stay below elastic rates. Radiative channels become more relevant at large momenta but these are thermally suppressed. At μ_B=0, η/s, ζ/s, and σ_Q/T agree with lattice QCD within uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: Inelastic gluon-radiation processes moderately reduce QGP transport coefficients. The extended DQPM framework provides predictions for finite μ_B relevant for beam-energy-scan programs, with baseline validation at μ_B=0 against lattice QCD.

title: Scalar Quantum Fields: Theory Space and its Geometry
comment: 27 pages, 5 figures, 1 table; author-prepared initial draft of chapter for forthcoming combined volume Comprehensive Quantum Physics; based on lectures delivered by one of the authors at BUSSTEPP 2025, University of Nottingham; comments welcome
summary: Scalar fields provide perhaps the simplest playground in which to develop our understanding of quantum field theory. In this lecture, we consider what it means to write down a scalar quantum field theory and how we can give geometrical interpretations to the space of such theories: the theory space.

AI.tldr: This lecture explores how scalar fields form a foundational framework for understanding quantum field theory, with a focus on defining what constitutes a scalar quantum field theory and interpreting the geometric structure of theory space.
AI.motivation: To develop a deeper understanding of quantum field theory by starting with the simplest case—scalar fields—and to provide a geometric interpretation of the space of possible theories.
AI.method: Conceptual analysis and pedagogical exposition of scalar quantum field theory, emphasizing geometric interpretations of theory space.
AI.result: A geometric perspective on theory space is developed, enabling the interpretation of scalar field theories as points or regions in a structured manifold.
AI.conclusion: Scalar fields serve as a useful toy model for exploring the structure of quantum field theory, and theory space can be given meaningful geometric interpretations.

title: Decays of heavy scalars in the Grimus-Neufeld model
summary: We consider an extension of the Standard Model by an additional Higgs doublet and a Majorana neutrino, which we call the Grimus-Neufeld Model (GNM). For certain parameter choices the GNM can be compared to the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), which has a scalar dark matter candidate. This motivates that the scalars of the GNM could possibly contribute to dark matter. To check this, we present the tree-level two-body decays of the heavy scalars of the GNM and compute the lifetime of the pseudoscalar in the IDM limit.

AI.tldr: The paper studies an extension of the Standard Model called the Grimus-Neufeld Model (GNM) with an extra Higgs doublet and a Majorana neutrino, compares it to the Inert Doublet Model (IDM) which has a scalar dark matter candidate, and analyzes whether GNM scalars could contribute to dark matter by examining their decays and lifetimes.
